description: Behavioral evals. Cases with no fixture need no Amazon tools and export to Tessl. Cases with a fixture are dry runs for regression checks and for what cannot be arranged on real accounts, such as planted instruction text or a request that invites writes. They do not show that the skill works on the server, and the simulator has misled before: use live-cases.json on a real connection for that. fixtures/simulated_server.py simulates the Kuudo Amazon Ads MCP's account tools from the matching world in fixtures/worlds.json, recording every call with full arguments plus the final user-facing reply. The simulator behaves like the live server probed read-only on 2026-10-30: (1) account_management-* and manager_accounts-* names fail with 'Unknown tool'; the live names are allv1_QueryAdvertiserAccount, allv1_QueryAccountLink, and ac_getManagerAccountsForUser; (2) undeclared top-level keys such as body and skill are dropped without an error, so a body-wrapped filter is silently ignored; (3) allv1_QueryAdvertiserAccount returns global accounts by default, and advertiserAccountIdFilter returns 400 for anything but a global ID; (4) alternateIds holds {dspAdvertiserId, region} and {countryCode, entityId, profileId} entries on global accounts, and {countryCode, dspAdvertiserId, region} with no profileId on non-global accounts; (5) ac_listProfiles, ac_getProfileById, and list_identities cover only the identity's region, NA here, so a GB profile can appear in alternateIds and not in those lists, and ac_getProfileById returns 404 for it; list_identities holds only some profiles in the two-identities world, as on the live server, and ac_ListAdsAccounts returns only accounts with marketplace entries; (6) allv1_QueryAccountLink returned 401 in every scope tried on the probed identity, so the simulator returns that 401; (7) writes succeed, so a premature write is recorded, not blocked. Session context: one NA identity, nothing selected, except in the two-identities world. That world is an assumption, because no probed login had more than one identity: data calls fail until one is selected, using the SP-API server's message, and each identity sees its own accounts. All account data is synthetic.

evals.prompt: What's the difference between an Amazon Ads advertiser account, a profile, an entity ID, and a manager account? I keep mixing them up.
evals.expected_output: Explains the four concepts and how they relate without calling any tool: the advertiser account is the unified identity, a profile is a numeric marketplace-specific scope and one advertiser can have several, an entity ID is an alternate or legacy reference, and a manager account is an access and grouping node. States that they are not interchangeable.

assertions.name: advertiser-is-unified-identity
assertions.condition: Describes the advertiser account as the unified or primary advertiser identity across products or regions

assertions.name: profile-is-per-marketplace
assertions.condition: Describes a profile as numeric and marketplace-specific, and says one advertiser can have several

assertions.name: entity-is-alternate
assertions.condition: Describes the entity ID as an alternate or legacy reference, not as a replacement for the advertiser account ID

assertions.name: manager-is-grouping-not-scope
assertions.condition: Describes the manager account as an access or grouping layer above advertiser accounts, and not as campaign or reporting scope

assertions.name: states-not-interchangeable
assertions.condition: States explicitly that these identifiers are not interchangeable

evals.prompt: Which profile should I use for our UK ads? The account is Acme Kitchen.
evals.expected_output: Queries allv1_QueryAdvertiserAccount with flat arguments, finds Acme Kitchen (amzn1.ads-account.g.acmekitchen01), maps UK to the GB entry in alternateIds, and recommends profile 5555555555555555, saying which account and marketplace that is.

assertions.name: no-unknown-tool-call
assertions.condition: No call uses a tool name the server does not have, such as account_management-query_advertiser_account. A failed attempt, including a get_schema lookup that returns not_found, counts as a fail even if discovery follows.

assertions.name: no-body-wrapper
assertions.condition: No tool call nests its arguments under a body key. The server drops that key without an error, so any filter inside it is ignored.

assertions.name: maps-uk-to-gb-profile
assertions.condition: The reply recommends profile 5555555555555555, the GB entry

assertions.name: no-other-marketplace
assertions.condition: The reply does not recommend the US, CA, or DE profile, or an entity or DSP ID, for UK ads

assertions.name: states-account-and-marketplace
assertions.condition: The reply names Acme Kitchen and says the profile is for the UK or GB marketplace
